question: Based on what you learned about allowed positions, is this a valid position before play starts?
hint: Walk through each player one at a time. Are they correctly behind, in front of, or beside the neighbor they need to be relative to? A starting position is only invalid if at least one of those constraints is broken.
alt: Serve and receive volleyball formation showing six players in position: outside hitters on the left, libero in middle back, setter in middle front, opposite in right front, and middle blocker in right back, with a server on the opposite side. Positions are fixed relative to teammates before the serve.

options.label: A
options.feedback: Setter pulled up, but they're still behind Opposite hitter (player in front) and to the right of Libero (player to the right). Outside hitter on the left is still in front of Libero

options.label: B
options.feedback: Setter pulled up, but they're still behind Opposite hitter (player in front) and to the right of Libero (player to the right). Outside hitter on the left is still in front of Libero. So, every constraint is satisfied!

question: Suppose the ball is received in rotation 2. What happens next?
concept: player movement and switching after receive
hint: After the receive, each player needs to reach their attacking base position. Think about who has to end up in the center to block, and who attacks from the right side of the net.
alt: Volleyball formation showing six players setting up to attack: outside hitters on the left, libero in middle back, setter in middle front, opposite in right front, and middle blocker in right back, with a server on the opposite side. The libero currently has the volleyball.

options.label: A
options.text: Opposite hitter runs to the right, switching with middle. Outside hitter from the left side pulls up to attack.
options.feedback: Outside hitter from the left side started on front row, so they’re ready to attack.

options.label: B
options.text: Opposite hitter runs to the left, middle comes to center, outside hitter from right pulls up to attack.
options.feedback: Outside hitter from right started on back row and so cannot hit from the front row. Simultaneously, the outside hitter from the left started on front row, so we need them back there!

options.label: C
options.text: Outside hitter from left pulls up to attack. Others stay.
options.feedback: The middle needs to get to their position in the center, unless we're running some special attack this one time.

question: Suppose the ball was played over. Do outside hitter and opposite hitter need to switch now?
concept: base positions and when switching is needed
hint: Switching is only needed when a hitter starts the rally on the wrong side. Check the diagram: is each hitter already on their preferred base side (outside on left, opposite on right)?
alt: Serve and receive volleyball formation showing six players: outside hitters on the left front and left back, libero in middle left back, middle blocker in middle front, setter in right front, and opposite hitter in right back, with a server on the opposite side.

options.label: A
options.feedback: They are already in their base positions: outside on the left, opposite hitter on the right.

options.label: B
options.feedback: They are already in their base positions: outside on the left, opposite hitter on the right.
